chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Tenor players: Ben Webster, Don Byas, Paul Gonsalves
summary: Webster was a disciple of Hawkins; Don Byas took over on the 1950-51 European tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, Ben? Ben was a disciple of Coleman Hawkins, as most every tenor player was and Ben loved Coleman and he attempted Coleman's lush, deep tone and, of course, they put themselves in with what they heard. And Ben was
very good, very good. He was one of the giants, we called them. But there was several of them around, in those days. And, --

Well, there was the boy in Europe. I'm speaking of Don Byas, something happened and Ben Webster couldn't go in '50 or '51, I think it was. So we contacted Don Byas and took him on the concert tour with us in Europe and, truthfully, Don Byas was a second attraction to that whole band. He played so much tenor that it was a shame, we should've left him home. Yeah, he really took over. Terrific, had known
You (inaudible) Don Byas in this country?
Oh, yes, yes. He was working down on 52nd Street, incidentally, with Coleman Hawkins several years before that and then he moved to Europe.
He was a good friend of the band, wasn't he?
I've heard a lot of very affectionate references to --
Oh, yes, he was another terrific, he -- there was so many fine, fine musicians in those days that it was a pleasure to know them.
It was along about that time that

Paul came a little later. He came over here. I never knew too much about Paul. But he was very good, he fit perfectly, came right along and everyone -- he had a beautiful personality. Beautiful personality. Getting a little heavy on the stand once in awhile. But, beautiful personality.
